audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Sett Level 1 and Level 6 and called first item and 2+ items skill fights, while every content why says level 1 is even, level 6 is even, and both item stages are Zaahen's — which is the packet chart.
audit.why: Sett wins this at only 47.69%, and Zaahen's Determination passive plus his healing Q and R take over once he has items.
audit.corrected: Skill / Sett / Sett / Skill / Skill / Zaahen / Zaahen.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four full-layer whys described Sett-favoured spikes in rows that are even or Zaahen's, and the packet flagged zero cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere in the matchup.
audit.why: The real timings are Grim Deliverance (R) at 110/95/80s and 600 range, Aureate Rush (E) at 10 down to 8s, and The Darkin Glaive (Q) at 10 down to 6s. None of them appeared.
audit.corrected: Whys rewritten to their real owners with the cooldowns that justify them, and breakdown.cooldowns rebuilt around all three.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every reference to Zaahen's kit was the placeholder word 'Ultimate' — including a breakdown.cooldowns entry reading 'Zaahen Ultimate (verify): His power spike — verify the exact name + effect on the live patch', which shipped to the page.
audit.why: The real names are available: The Darkin Glaive (Q), Aureate Rush (E) and Grim Deliverance (R). The Darkin Glaive is an auto reset that heals and whose recast knocks up; Aureate Rush is a percent-health dash, so armour reads that trade wrong; Grim Deliverance heals him off the damage it deals.
audit.corrected: Placeholders replaced with real names, the auto-reset tell, the percent-health note and the anti-heal timing.
sources: _missing/sett.json key 57 (names The Darkin Glaive, Aureate Rush, Grim Deliverance)

edits.before: Double-punch passive makes you the strongest level-1 auto-trader in the lane. Punish Zaahen on every CS, but respect his opening tool — chips now, all-ins later.
edits.after: Level 1 is even. The Darkin Glaive (Q) is an auto reset that heals him, so trade on his wind-up, not after it, and do not chase him through the double slash.

edits.before: The Show Stopper online — you can start fights Zaahen doesn't want. Suplex him into your wave or tower, never into his own minions.
edits.after: Both ults land at 6: yours is 120s, Grim Deliverance is 110s and heals him off the damage. Whoever engages better takes the stage.

edits.before: Stridebreaker fixes your only weakness — sticking to Zaahen. Shove, recall on the spike, and force the next trade before he matches your item.
edits.after: His first item is the turn: Determination stacks into bonus AD and a revive, and Grim Deliverance heals him through your Haymaker.

edits.before: Sterak's makes your all-in nearly unburstable. Fights are decided by whether you cash a max-grit W — track Ultimate and commit on the gap.
edits.after: Two items in, Aureate Rush (E) deals percent health on an 8s dash — armour does not read that trade. Avoid the sidelane duel.

edits.before: - Zaahen Ultimate: matchup-defining — His big cooldown. All-in when it’s down. Track it before every engage. - Zaahen Ultimate (verify): His power spike — verify the exact name + effect on the live patch. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Zaahen Grim Deliverance (R): 110s, 600 range — it heals him off the damage, so anti-heal before you commit. - Aureate Rush (E): 10s to 8s, a dash that deals percent health. - The Darkin Glaive (Q): 10s to 6s, auto reset, recast knocks up.

edits.before: New-champ respect — bait his cooldown, then E-stun all-in. Sett wins by trading around Zaahen's Ultimate and cashing the pattern: bait his key tool, then all-in.
edits.after: Bait The Darkin Glaive (Q) — it is an auto reset, so the wind-up is the tell. Sett owns levels 2-3; Zaahen owns the game from his first item, so cash the lead early.

edits.before: Extended brawls his passive heals through
edits.after: Extended brawls his Q and R heal through

notes: Zaahen's abilities were referenced only as the placeholder 'Ultimate', and one breakdown.cooldowns line literally told the reader to go verify the ability name on the live patch. Ability names came from the _missing interactions file (The Darkin Glaive, Aureate Rush, Grim Deliverance); the packet's enemyAbilities block is null and Zaahen's W and passive names are still unknown, so neither was named. Confidence on the naming is Medium for that reason.
